title: Lifting the degeneracy of quantum spin liquid phase by uniaxial pressure
authors: Shams Sohel Islam, Zurab Guguchia, Orion Gerguri, Petr Král, Maxime Lamotte, Toni Shiroka, Jonas A. Krieger, Thomas J. Hicken, Tina Arh, Gediminas Simutis, Abanoub Hanna, Nazmul Islam, Bella Lake, Hubertus Luetkens, Hans Henning Klauss, Rajib Sarkar
abstract: We report muon spin relaxation/rotation ($μ$SR) measurements of the candidate three-dimensional (3D) quantum spin liquid (QSL) PbCuTe$_2$O$_6$, hosting $S=1/2$ moments, under controlled in situ [110] uniaxial compression up to $σ_{[110]}=37.7$~MPa. A small directional lattice perturbation significantly modifies the local magnetic response, while above $σ_{\rm cr}\sim10.8$\,MPa the relaxation rates are strongly enhanced and the internal-field distribution is substantially broadened. These changes occur along with the local crystalline symmetry breaking. While, no evidence for conventional static long-range magnetic order is observed, the compression drives the system towards a structurally modified and strongly correlated state in which enhanced quasi-static correlations coexist with persistent slow spin dynamics. This work demonstrates a clean and symmetry-selective route to control frustrated exchange landscape and access hidden magnetic instabilities in a 3D QSL candidate opening up the possibilities to tune other correlated systems where intrinsic coupling between magnetic and lattice degrees of freedom are relevant.
summary: This work uses muon spin relaxation ($\mu$SR) under uniaxial pressure to probe the quantum spin liquid candidate $	ext{PbCuTe}_2	ext{O}_6$. The researchers found that applying stress modifies the local magnetic response and enhances quasi-static correlations without inducing conventional long-range magnetic order. This demonstrates a powerful, symmetry-selective method for controlling frustrated exchange interactions in QSL materials.
main_problem: To determine if uniaxial pressure can control the frustrated exchange landscape of a 3D Quantum Spin Liquid (QSL) candidate, $	ext{PbCuTe}_2	ext{O}_6$, and potentially drive it toward magnetic order.
main_result: The system remains in a dynamically fluctuating state even under high stress, but compression provides a clean route to tune the frustrated exchange landscape by exploiting magnetoelastic coupling. No evidence for conventional static long-range magnetic order was observed.
method: Muon spin relaxation/rotation ($\mu$SR) measurements were performed *in situ* while applying controlled uniaxial compression along the [110] direction.
model_or_system: The study investigates $	ext{PbCuTe}_2	ext{O}_6$, a candidate three-dimensional (3D) $S=1/2$ QSL characterized by competing antiferromagnetic interactions forming a frustrated 3D hyper-hyperkagome network.
key_observables: Muon spin relaxation rates ($\lambda_{	ext{fast}}, \lambda_{	ext{slow}}$), internal-field distribution broadening, and the stress-strain curve.
important_parameters: Uniaxial stress $\sigma_{[110]}$ up to $37.7\ 	ext{MPa}$; critical stress $\sigma_{	ext{cr}} \sim 10.8\ 	ext{MPa}$.
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes that the observed changes are due to magnetoelastic coupling between lattice strain and magnetic correlations.
figures_summary: Figures show ZF-$\mu$SR spectra, force-displacement curves correlating stress with $\mu$SR response, and temperature dependence of relaxation rates under varying uniaxial stresses.
paper_structure: The paper systematically measures $\mu$SR properties across a range of applied uniaxial stresses, identifying critical structural transitions ($\sigma_{	ext{cr}}$) that correlate with changes in the local magnetic environment and spin dynamics.
why_interesting: The ability to tune quantum magnetic ground states using external strain is highly relevant for understanding emergent phenomena in strongly correlated electron systems, providing a clean experimental handle on frustrated interactions.
